title: How to Start a Cat Cafe: Costs, Steps, and Risks
summary: How to start a cat cafe: get startup cost ranges, licensing rules, labor budgets, and why some close. Follow our 8 steps plus a pre-opening checklist.
body_markdown:
A cat cafe looks simple from the outside: coffee, a calm room, and a few cats. Behind the counter, you’re running a cafe and an animal care operation at the same time. That means two sets of costs, two sets of rules, and a team that needs both skills. This guide on how to start a cat cafe covers what it costs, why some close, and the eight steps to open one.


## **In Short: How to Start a Cat Cafe**


**Here’s how to start a cat cafe:** check your local licensing rules first, budget roughly $25,000 to $300,000 for startup costs, and set your labor target before you sign a lease.


- **Cost:** Lean models that partner with a nearby cafe sit at the low end. Full build-outs with a kitchen sit at the high end.
- **Licensing:** Rules are local, so start with a call to your health department.
- **Profit:** Margins run thin, and labor is the cost you control most.
- **The eight steps:** Plan, license, locate, design, source cats, budget, hire, and market.

## **What Is a Cat Cafe?**


A cat cafe is a coffee shop where guests spend time with cats while they eat and drink. The idea started in Taiwan in 1998, and there are now more than 200 in the US, according to[USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/pets/2025/01/24/cat-cafe-rescue-animals-rise-in-popularity-adoptions/77877166007/) . Most follow one of two models:


- **Rescue partnership:** A shelter or rescue owns the cats, and guests can apply to adopt them.
- **Resident cats:** The cafe owns its cats, and they live there long term.


Guests usually pay for drinks plus a separate fee for time with the cats. Crumbs & Whiskers in Washington, DC charges $18 to $22 for a 70-minute visit, according to[TRUiC](https://truicbusinessideas.com/cat-cafe) .


## **How Much Does It Cost to Start a Cat Cafe?**


**Startup costs for a cat cafe run from about $25,000 to $300,000, depending on your model, city, and space.** TRUiC estimates $25,000 to $250,000, and[Myshyft](https://www.myshyft.com/blog/how-to-start-a-cat-cafe/) estimates $50,000 to $300,000. Your lease, renovations for health code separation, and kitchen equipment drive most of the total.


Your model sets where you land in that range:


- **Lean:** Packaged food only, or a partnership with a nearby cafe. Cost drivers: smaller build-out, no kitchen equipment.
- **Mid:** A small on-site kitchen and a separate cat room. Cost drivers: kitchen equipment and a second room.
- **Full:** An in-house kitchen, full separation, a larger space. Cost drivers: a bigger lease and build-out.


Crumbs & Whiskers kept costs down by having a team member pick up food and drinks from a nearby cafe, according to TRUiC. Lazy Cat Cafe Downtown in Toronto cited about $10,000 in monthly rent and roughly $5,000 a month in vet bills when it announced its closure in 2025, according to[BlogTO](https://blogto.com/eat_drink/2025/01/lazy-cat-cafe-toronto-closing) . Add vet care, extra cleaning, and insurance to your monthly budget.


For a wider look at what any new business costs, see our guide to[how much it costs to start a business](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-much-does-it-cost-to-start-a-business) .


## **Are Cat Cafes Profitable?**


**Cat cafes can be profitable, but margins run thin.** TRUiC estimates a net profit margin near 3% and a break-even point of four to 12 months. Admission fees, events, memberships, and adoption fees give you more ways to cover costs than drinks alone.


Labor is the cost you can control. Coffee shop operators often aim for labor at 30% to 35% of sales, according to Lavu. Say your monthly payroll is $8,000 to $15,000. At that target, you need roughly $23,000 to $50,000 in monthly sales to support it. Treat that as an illustration, and set your labor target before you open.

Once you’re open, our[time clock](https://www.joinhomebase.com/time-clock) tracks labor cost by hour, department, and role, so you can see where you stand. Calvin Su, co-owner of Butter Baker, says: “I think it’s great for planning, for budgeting… with the labor cost keep going up, it really helps us to track.”


## **Why Are Cat Cafes Closing Down?**


**Most cat cafes close because costs outrun sales.** Rent, vet bills, and slow months add up fast, and some owners also run into inspection problems or run low on adoptable cats. You can plan for most of these risks before you open.


- **Rent and vet bills:** Lazy Cat Cafe Downtown cited both when it announced its 2025 closure.
- **Slow months:** South Paw Cat Cafe closed after two slow months, according to Kingstonist.
- **Running out of cats:** Vancouver’s Catfe closed temporarily soon after opening because adoptions left it without cats, according to NPR.
- **Compliance:** Tokyo’s government shut a cat cafe for 30 days over hygiene and nutrition standards for its cats, according to Fox News.


## **How to Start a Cat Cafe in 8 Steps**


Once you’ve weighed the costs and risks, these eight steps take you from business plan to opening day.


### **1. Create Your Cat Cafe Business Plan**


Your business plan is your roadmap, even if you’re not seeking investors. Cover your market, your competitors, what makes your cafe different, and projections for both cafe and cat care costs. Choose your cat model and decide whether to open on your own or buy into a franchise. Our guide to[starting a small business](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-start-a-small-business) covers the basics.


### **2. Check Your Licensing and Health Code Rules**


Yes, you need licenses and permits, and you should check them before you sign a lease. The[FDA Food Code](https://www.fda.gov/media/164194/download) says live animals may not be on the premises of a food establishment, with limited exceptions. States adopt that rule themselves, and Washington’s version is[WAC 246-215-06570](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/washington/WAC-246-215-06570) . Cat cafes operate through exceptions, variances, or layouts that keep cats away from food.


Local officials decide how that works. In Keene, New Hampshire, a health official said the city’s food code has no section on cat cafes, and he can grant an exception if owners keep cats and food separate, according to[the Keene Sentinel](https://www.keenesentinel.com/eedition/page-a3/page_33a2b9a7-f86a-579f-aa84-610b5ae31d38.html) . Before you sign a lease, ask your health department:


1. Do I need an exception or variance to have cats on the premises?
2. Are packaged food and drinks treated differently from food prepared on site?
3. What separation does my layout need between the cat area and the food area?


You may also need a business license, a food handler permit for each team member, and an animal permit. With our[HR and compliance tools](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hr-compliance) , you can store permits and training records in each team member’s profile for inspections.


### **3. Find a Location**


Look for foot traffic and a layout with room for separate zones. Kate, who owns Kitty Cafe, recommends three areas: one for guests to play with cats, one where cats can rest, and a food prep area if you cook on site, according to TRUiC. Confirm the zoning allows both food service and animals before you sign.


### **4. Design Your Space**


Your space has to work for cats, guests, and inspectors. Many cafes keep the cat room separate and let guests look in through a window, according to Shopify. Put litter boxes in a cat-only zone, and plan an entry that keeps cats from slipping out. Add climbing spaces and hiding spots so shy cats can retreat.


### **5. Source Your Cats**


You can partner with a local rescue or own your cats. Rescue partnerships lower your upfront costs and let you offer adoptions. Owned cats give you consistency, but you’re responsible for their vet care long term.


Some shelters limit how many cats you can take or ask to approve your space, according to Shopify. If you partner with a rescue, line up a steady supply. Plan quiet rest areas, too, because cats need breaks from guests.


### **6. Set Your Budget and Get Insured**


Use your cost table to set a startup budget and a monthly operating budget. The[SBA’s startup cost tool](https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/plan-your-business/calculate-your-startup-costs) helps you build both. If your projections show you running out of cash before break-even,[raise more money](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-get-a-loan-to-start-a-business) or scale back your concept. Get general liability insurance, and workers’ compensation if you have a team, according to TRUiC.


### **7. Build Your Cat Cafe Team**


Most cat cafes need cafe roles and cat care roles. A barista makes drinks, a cashier handles orders, and someone who loves cats handles cleaning and care, according to Shopify. Team members can rotate, but each shift needs coverage for both.


Here’s what that costs. The[Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/food-preparation-and-serving/food-and-beverage-serving-and-related-workers.htm) puts the median wage for food and beverage serving workers at $15.24 an hour (May 2025). One barista, one cashier, and one cat attendant working eight hours a day for 30 days adds up to 720 hours, or about $10,970 in base wages. That’s before payroll taxes, a manager, a second shift, or higher city wages.


When you[hire your first team members](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/hiring-your-first-employee) , look for shelter or rescue experience. Every team member needs a food handler permit and basic cat handling training. Peak cafe hours and peak cat time don’t always line up, so build[role-based schedules](https://www.joinhomebase.com/employee-scheduling) , post open shifts, and let your team trade shifts.


Roberto Bustillos of Lombard Doggy Daycare says the app eased his early worry: “My biggest fear at the beginning was I’m getting into a very complicated business… how to manage the schedules, how to deal with payroll. All of that was so simple.”


### **8. Market Your Cat Cafe**


Start building buzz before you open. Introduce your cats on Instagram, partner with local rescues for pre-opening adoption events, and invite local press. Events like happy hours, yoga classes, and casual concerts give guests reasons to return, according to Shopify. Cats won’t market themselves, so plan your content early.


## **Is a Cat Cafe Right for You?**


A cat cafe is a full-time commitment, and TRUiC describes it as part cafe and part animal shelter. You’re a good fit if you:


- Have food service or operations experience.
- Can handle the emotional side of rescue partnerships.
- Enjoy community building and constant marketing.
- Have a cash cushion beyond your startup budget.


It’s probably not a fit if you expect passive income or want to avoid regulations.


## **Cat Cafe Pre-Opening Checklist**


- Call your health department and animal control to confirm permits and exceptions.
- Get your business license, food service permit, and any animal permit.
- Collect food handler permits and cat handling training records.
- Line up a vet partner and a source of cats.
- Buy liability insurance, plus workers’ compensation if you have a team.
- Set your labor target and build your first schedule.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Starting a Cat Cafe**


### **How Much Does It Cost to Start a Cat Cafe?**


Startup costs run from about $25,000 for a lean setup that partners with a nearby cafe to $250,000 or more for a full build-out with an in-house kitchen. Rent, renovations for health code separation, and kitchen equipment drive most of the total. Get local quotes before you commit to a lease.


### **Why Are Cat Cafes Closing Down?**


Most closures come from costs outrunning sales. Toronto’s Lazy Cat Cafe Downtown cited about $10,000 in monthly rent and roughly $5,000 in vet bills when it announced its 2025 closure. Slow months, strict inspections, and running low on adoptable cats have also forced owners to close or pause.


### **Do You Need a License to Own a Cat Cafe?**


Yes. You need a general business license and a food service permit from your local health department. Many areas also require an animal permit or a health department exception, since the FDA Food Code bars live animals from food establishments by default. Rules vary by city and state, so ask both offices before you sign a lease.


### **Are Cat Cafes Profitable?**


They can be, but margins run thin. TRUiC estimates a net profit margin near 3%, and costs run higher than a standard cafe because of vet care, extra cleaning, and cat attendants. Cafes that earn from admission fees, events, and memberships, not just drinks, have more room to cover those costs.


### **Can You Adopt Cats from a Cat Cafe?**


At many cat cafes, yes. Cafes that partner with a shelter or rescue let visitors apply to adopt the cats they meet, usually through an application and an interview with the team. Resident-cat cafes keep their cats long term. Ask the cafe which model it follows before you apply.


### **How Many Cats Does a Cat Cafe Need?**


Most cat cafes keep roughly 10 to 25 cats, though local rules may cap the number. Neko Cat Cafe in Washington rotates 12 to 25 cats, while one New Hampshire cafe planned for up to 10 at a time. Check your local limits, then plan space and rest areas around your count.


## **Ready to Start Your Cat Cafe?**


A cat cafe works when the numbers, the rules, and the team line up. Cost your model first, check licensing before you lease, and set your labor target early.
